text:
ConocoPhillips rose 1.83% today to $140.08, continuing a sharp two-week rally that's now up 11.67%. The stock is riding a wave driven by oil price volatility: while U.S. crude sits at $96.24 per barrel, global Brent crude has spiked to $125.44, creating a wide price gap that benefits large integrated oil producers with global operations. Recent geopolitical tensions — potential U.S. strikes on Iran, Saudi airport attacks, and Houthi attacks on shipping lanes — have kept crude elevated despite headlines about Russian diesel entering markets, which might otherwise have capped prices.

The broader context is that energy markets are pricing in real supply-risk premium right now. Disruptions to Middle Eastern oil flows (whether from Iran, Saudi Arabia, or the Houthi threat to Red Sea shipping) matter far more to global prices than the modest volume of Russian diesel the Trump administration is negotiating, so crude has stayed firm enough to support oil-stock gains.
